correctness.rationale: For a complex 2x2 input A, write a=tr(A)/2 and T=A-aI with singular values s>=t. The support-function calculation characterizes a circular numerical range centered c of radius r>0 exactly by cI+N, N^2=0, ||N||_F=2r. The traceless identity T*T+TT*=(s^2+t^2)I ensures a top right singular vector v can be chosen with v*Tv=0, so u=Tv/s is perpendicular to v and saturates the Frobenius inner-product bound. Thus min squared distance equals 2|a-c|^2+t^2+(s-2r)^2. The simple top singular ray for s>t yields uniqueness, while normal/scalar cases yield continuous minimizers; a real perpendicular singular pair exists when A,c are real. Minimizing the square in r and then c proves the stated corollaries. Independent code checked 100 random complex instances for nilpotency, geometry, orthogonality and distance; finite checks are corroborative only.
residual_risks: Independent bounded calculations corroborate but do not prove infinite quantifiers; the reviewed mathematical proof is the universal argument.
